_meta.description: Victorian Curriculum 2.0 content descriptions for Science, Design and Technologies and Digital Technologies, Foundation to Level 6, for choosing curriculum targets when planning.
_meta.source: Codes, strands and sub-strands from f10.vcaa.vic.edu.au, read on 2026-11-04.
_meta.wording: Each summary is a short paraphrase in our own words. The official wording is owned by the VCAA and stays on its site: every code links there.
_meta.pairs: Science Understanding and Design and Technologies (Technologies Contexts) codes that genuinely connect: the knowledge in one is what students use in the other. Written by Claude for James (November 2026) as a starting point for planning; Claude judges the fit for each unit.

VC2TDE2S01.summary: How people design and make familiar products, services and places to meet local needs, including sustainability.

VC2TDE2C01.summary: How technologies make things move in products and systems.

VC2TDE2C02.summary: How plants and animals are grown for food, clothing and shelter.

VC2TDE2C03.summary: Choosing and preparing food for healthy eating.

VC2TDE2C04.summary: The characteristics and properties of materials and components used in designs.

VC2TDE2D01.summary: Explore a need, and the materials, tools and processes to design for it.

VC2TDE2D02.summary: Come up with and share design ideas by describing, drawing or modelling, with hand and digital tools.

VC2TDE2D03.summary: Use materials, tools and techniques to make designs safely.

VC2TDE2D04.summary: Describe and choose design ideas by personal preference, including sustainability.

VC2TDE2D05.summary: Put the steps for making a design in order, working together.

VC2TDE4S01.summary: People in design jobs, and what (including sustainability) shapes designs for community needs.

VC2TDE4C01.summary: How forces affect the way a product or system works.

VC2TDE4C02.summary: Ways food and fibre are produced.

VC2TDE4C03.summary: Ways to choose and prepare food for healthy eating.

VC2TDE4C04.summary: How material properties affect the way a product or system works.

VC2TDE4D01.summary: Explore a need, and design and test the materials, tools and processes for it.

VC2TDE4D02.summary: Develop and share design ideas with technical words and drawings, by hand or digitally.

VC2TDE4D03.summary: Choose and use materials, tools and techniques to make designs safely.

VC2TDE4D04.summary: Judge design ideas and solutions against given criteria, including sustainability.

VC2TDE4D05.summary: Plan the steps to make a design, alone and in a team.

VC2TDE6S01.summary: How designers weigh up competing ethical factors, including sustainability, in products, services and places.

VC2TDE6C01.summary: How electrical energy becomes movement, sound or light in a product or system.

VC2TDE6C02.summary: How and why food and fibre are produced in managed environments.

VC2TDE6C03.summary: How the properties of foods affect choosing and preparing them for healthy eating.

VC2TDE6C04.summary: How the properties of materials, systems, components and tools affect how they are used to make designs.

VC2TDE6D01.summary: Investigate a need, and the materials, tools and processes to design for it.

VC2TDE6D02.summary: Develop, improve and share design ideas with technical words and drawings, by hand or digitally.

VC2TDE6D03.summary: Choose, explain and use suitable materials, tools and techniques to make designs safely.

VC2TDE6D04.summary: Agree on design criteria, including ethics and sustainability, and use them to evaluate.

VC2TDE6D05.summary: Write project plans that account for resources, alone and in a team.

VC2TDI2S01.summary: Explore digital systems and their hardware and software parts.

VC2TDI2S02.summary: Know some data is personal, and log in to a school account.

VC2TDI2D01.summary: Find patterns in data and show data as objects, pictures, symbols, numbers and words.

VC2TDI2D02.summary: Use basic features of digital tools to make, find and share content for an audience.

VC2TDI2D03.summary: Use digital tools to share and work together safely, with a trusted adult.

VC2TDI2D04.summary: Talk about how some websites and apps keep personal data online.

VC2TDI2C01.summary: Look at simple problems that a digital system could solve for someone.

VC2TDI2C02.summary: Follow, describe and show algorithms with steps, decisions (branching) and repeats.

VC2TDI2C03.summary: Talk about how digital systems meet people's needs.

VC2TDI4S01.summary: Describe different digital systems and the devices connected to them.

VC2TDI4S02.summary: Explore sending different kinds of data between digital systems.

VC2TDI4S03.summary: Use a memorised password and explain what makes a good one.

VC2TDI4D01.summary: Recognise types of data and how the same data can be shown in different ways.

VC2TDI4D02.summary: Collect, organise and present data with software to solve problems.

VC2TDI4D03.summary: Use core features of digital tools to make, find and share content for an audience.

VC2TDI4D04.summary: Use digital tools to share, plan and work together safely.

VC2TDI4D05.summary: Know what personal data online accounts hold and talk about the risks.

VC2TDI4C01.summary: Define simple problems from requirements the teacher gives.

VC2TDI4C02.summary: Follow, describe and show algorithms with sequence, comparisons (branching) and repeats.

VC2TDI4C03.summary: Design a simple user interface, then share and compare designs.

VC2TDI4C04.summary: Build simple algorithms as visual programs with control structures and input.

VC2TDI4C05.summary: Talk about how existing and their own solutions meet the requirements.

VC2TDI6S01.summary: Investigate the main parts inside digital systems and what they do.

VC2TDI6S02.summary: Examine how digital systems connect in networks to send data.

VC2TDI6S03.summary: Use different passphrases for different accounts and explain the risk of reusing them.

VC2TDI6D01.summary: Explain that digital systems store data as numbers, and explore binary.

VC2TDI6D02.summary: Gather and change data from different sources with software, including spreadsheets.

VC2TDI6D03.summary: Analyse and graph data with software, including spreadsheets, to solve problems.

VC2TDI6D04.summary: Choose and use digital tools well to make, find and share content for an audience.

VC2TDI6D05.summary: Choose and use digital tools to share online, plan and collaborate on projects safely.

VC2TDI6D06.summary: Explain their digital footprint and think about privacy when collecting personal data.

VC2TDI6C01.summary: Define problems from requirements the teacher gives or the class writes together.

VC2TDI6C02.summary: Design and show algorithms with several options (branching) and repeats.

VC2TDI6C03.summary: Design and change a user interface, then share and evaluate the designs.

VC2TDI6C04.summary: Build algorithms as visual programs with control structures, variables and input.

VC2TDI6C05.summary: Evaluate existing and their own solutions against requirements and their effect on the community.

VC2S2H01.summary: Science knowledge comes from observing the world with the senses and with tools.

VC2S2H02.summary: People use science every day, asking questions and using patterns to predict.

VC2S2U01.summary: Plants and animals have features we can see and use to group them.

VC2S2U02.summary: Living things need air, water, food and shelter, and their homes meet those needs.

VC2S2U03.summary: Parts of plants and animals have jobs that help them survive.

VC2S2U04.summary: Objects are made of one or more materials, and materials have properties we can observe.

VC2S2U05.summary: Materials can be combined for a purpose, and the result can have different properties from what it was made of.

VC2S2U06.summary: Bending, twisting, stretching, squashing or breaking changes a material's shape but not what it is made of.

VC2S2U07.summary: Daily and seasonal changes in weather affect everyday choices.

VC2S2U08.summary: Earth is one of 8 planets, and the Sun, Moon, planets and stars move in patterns across the sky.

VC2S2U09.summary: Caring for Earth's water, land and air by reducing, re-using and recycling.

VC2S2U10.summary: How an object moves depends on things like its size, shape and material.

VC2S2U11.summary: Pushes and pulls are forces that change how things move or their shape.

VC2S2U12.summary: Sound makes materials vibrate and vibrations make sound, with different pitch and volume.

VC2S2I01.summary: Ask questions and make predictions from what they have noticed.

VC2S2I02.summary: Investigate questions safely by following steps in order.

VC2S2I03.summary: Observe with the senses and record, including informal measuring, with digital tools if useful.

VC2S2I04.summary: Sort and order information with tables, organisers and models to show patterns.

VC2S2I05.summary: Compare what happened with predictions and with others, leading to new questions.

VC2S2I06.summary: Share observations and ideas with everyday and some science words.

VC2S4H01.summary: Data from investigations is used to explain natural events.

VC2S4H02.summary: People use science knowledge, skills and data to meet needs and solve problems.

VC2S4U01.summary: How living things differ from non-living things and once-living things, including fossils.

VC2S4U02.summary: Plants and animals have life cycles, and offspring are like but not the same as their parents.

VC2S4U03.summary: Consumers, producers and decomposers in a habitat, and food chains.

VC2S4U04.summary: Properties of solids, liquids and gases, and how heating or cooling changes state.

VC2S4U05.summary: The properties of natural and made materials affect how they are used and re-used.

VC2S4U06.summary: Rocks, minerals and soils are resources with properties that make them useful.

VC2S4U07.summary: Where water comes from and how it moves through the water cycle.

VC2S4U08.summary: Weather and climate affect land, air, water and living things, and people affect climate.

VC2S4U09.summary: Sources of heat, and how heat moves from one object to another.

VC2S4U10.summary: Friction, gravity, static and magnetic forces act by touch or at a distance and change speed and direction.

VC2S4I01.summary: Pose questions and predict outcomes from patterns they observe.

VC2S4I02.summary: Plan and carry out investigations with scaffolds, including fair tests and safety.

VC2S4I03.summary: Measure and record with familiar instruments and digital tools.

VC2S4I04.summary: Show patterns in data with tables, graphs and models.

VC2S4I05.summary: Compare findings with others, including whether a test was fair, to draw conclusions.

VC2S4I06.summary: Share findings with science words and digital tools for a purpose and audience.

VC2S6H01.summary: Science changes over time as scientists collaborate and build on each other's work.

VC2S6H02.summary: Communities use science to identify problems and make decisions.

VC2S6U01.summary: Habitats and their physical conditions, and how changes, including by people, affect living things.

VC2S6U02.summary: Living things have evolved, and their features and behaviours help them thrive.

VC2S6U03.summary: Particle models explain solids, liquids and gases, and mixing substances makes mixtures and solutions.

VC2S6U04.summary: Reversible changes (melting, dissolving) and irreversible changes that make new substances (cooking, rusting).

VC2S6U05.summary: Weathering, erosion and deposition change Earth's surface slowly or quickly.

VC2S6U06.summary: Natural hazards like earthquakes, eruptions, bushfires and floods, and how people reduce their impact.

VC2S6U07.summary: Gravity keeps planets orbiting the Sun, and Earth's tilt and spin explain day, night and seasons.

VC2S6U08.summary: Light travels in straight lines, makes shadows, and can be absorbed, reflected or refracted.

VC2S6U09.summary: Conductors and insulators, and how energy moves through the parts of an electrical circuit.

VC2S6I01.summary: Use testable questions and reasoned predictions to guide investigations.

VC2S6I02.summary: Plan and carry out repeatable fair tests, choosing variables and planning for safety and ethics.

VC2S6I03.summary: Use equipment to measure and record data accurately, with digital tools if useful.

VC2S6I04.summary: Show patterns, trends and relationships with tables, graphs and models.

VC2S6I05.summary: Compare methods and findings to spot errors and back up conclusions.

VC2S6I06.summary: Communicate science ideas and findings for a purpose and audience in different formats.

pairs.how: What living things need is what farmers and gardeners must give the plants and animals they grow.
The parts of plants and animals we eat or use (seeds, leaves, fruit, wool) each have a job for the living thing first.
Sorting plants and animals by their features leads into which ones people grow for food, clothing and shelter.
Students test the properties of materials, then choose the right material for each part of a design.
Combining materials (paper and glue, straw and clay) makes something with new properties a design can use.
Combining ingredients changes them, which is how simple healthy food is made.
Folding, rolling or twisting a material changes its shape and how strong it is, so designers shape materials on purpose.
The weather sets the design brief: a shelter or outfit needs waterproof, warm or shady materials.
Designing with re-used and recycled materials puts reduce, re-use and recycle into practice.
Changing an object's size, shape or material changes how it moves, which is how designers make a product move the way they want.
Pushes and pulls are what make a moving product or toy work.
Different materials vibrate differently, so the materials chosen decide how a home-made instrument sounds.
Growing food follows life cycles: seed to harvest, egg to hen, and farmers plan around them.
A farm or garden is a habitat: producers, consumers and decomposers (compost, worms, pests) all affect what it produces.
Heating and cooling change food's state (melting, freezing, setting), which is how many foods are prepared.
The properties of natural and made materials decide which material suits each part of a product.
Soil is the resource food grows in, and its properties affect what grows well.
Rocks, clay and soil are materials whose properties make them useful for building and making.
Food production depends on water: collecting rainwater, irrigation and keeping soil moist.
Weather and climate decide what can be grown where, and how farmers protect crops and animals.
How heat moves explains which materials insulate, so students can design something that keeps things hot or cold.
Heat moving into food is what cooks it, so heat transfer explains food preparation.
Friction, gravity and magnetic forces decide how a product moves, grips, slides or holds together.
Managed environments (farms, plantations, fisheries) change habitats, and producers design ways to reduce the harm.
Farmers choose and breed plants and animals for features that help them thrive in managed environments.
Animal and plant adaptations inspire designs (biomimicry), using materials that copy those features.
Many foods are mixtures and solutions, and their particle behaviour explains how they are prepared.
Cooking is an irreversible change, and choosing how to prepare food depends on which changes we want.
Knowing how weathering and erosion work lets students design and test structures and materials that slow them down.
Designing for natural hazards (fire, flood, earthquake) depends on the properties of materials and structures.
Seasons, caused by Earth's tilt, set the calendar for growing and producing food and fibre.
Whether a material lets light through, reflects or absorbs it decides how it is used in a design (shades, reflectors, windows).
Electrical energy turned into light is how torches and signals work, and how light travels decides where the light goes.
A circuit's conductors, insulators and components are what turn electrical energy into movement, sound or light in a product.
